risks.title: HRP risks
risks.note: Linking indicators to hazards is a team design decision; NASA does not classify them this way.
hazards.items.radiacion.resumen: Radiation is invisible and NASA considers it one of the most dangerous aspects of spaceflight.
hazards.items.radiacion.como: Logs cumulative dose as a percentage of the mission limit and alerts when approaching it.
Groups isolated in a small space for long periods show behavioral responses; crews are carefully selected, trained, and supported.
Tracks sleep hours and daily mood, offering private screening and a personal journal that never leaves the spacecraft.
hazards.items.distancia_tierra.resumen: The farther the crew travels, the harder it is to receive instructions, supplies, and medical care from Earth. NASA stresses planning and self-sufficiency.
hazards.items.distancia_tierra.como: Decides on board without waiting for Earth, queues messages during a blackout, and sends the most urgent ones first when the link returns.
hazards.items.campos_gravedad.resumen: The body must adapt to different gravity levels: the spacecraft, the Moon or Mars, and back to Earth on return.
hazards.items.campos_gravedad.como: Compares each person against their own rolling baseline, because what is normal in one gravity level is not in another.
hazards.items.entornos_hostiles_cerrados: Keeping a safe ecosystem inside the spacecraft is hard: temperature, pressure, light, noise, microbes, and immune responses all interact.
Monitors cabin CO₂, temperature, and oxygenation, and cross-checks cabin air with multiple crew members at once.
